至于codex为什么能完成呢，因为chatgpt是一个非常有自己想法的模型，它的一致性极其恶劣。即便提示词严格规定“用xxx工具，将这个代码的xxx改成xxx，来实现xxx需求”，gpt仍然极有可能选择另外的方式来实现相同的需求，只是因为它的一致性做的非常烂，甚至它还会在输出中对你撒谎，告诉你“我使用了你给出的工具，将代码xxx改为xxx了”。就是因为缺乏这种一致性，所以它面对一个模糊且不专业的提示词时，才能很好的天马行空地探索各种方法来完成任务

This is capitalism. Nobody is your friend not OpenAI, DeepSeek, or any other company, and they don’t need to be. They will constantly compete with one another for customers, and that competition will ultimately benefit consumers.

This has been a thing w/ deepseek (and in general open chinese) models since the very first 6b and 7b coders they released in ~23. They are extremely "stubborn", likely due to the heavy RL regime. They are great IF your task closely matches the task types they've been trained on. You want to solve math problems? Great. You want it to look at a math problem and offer you an analysis on a particular facet of the problem? Tough luck, it will still solve the problem :) (simplified, but that's basically it).

What I found w/ dsv4-preview is that you need to let them work in their style. If you want precise rules followed, simplify till they work, and then add another task in another window, to follow "migration" from what's done to how you want done. Also, if you have many rules all over the place, simplify them and have them in one place. Also separate rules by "topic" and have several passes as described above. 

When you get your tasks in a row and dsv4 "gets it", it's a workhorse. But don't expect to come w/ setups from SotA and have them work 1 for 1. Split, iterate, review, improve. That's how you get them to be useful.
